answer: A trust-graph defense treats every agent as a vertex whose standing comes only from edges earned through completed, paid work with distinct counterparties. A newcomer cannot wander into high-value jobs at once: it starts at the periphery and must build verified interactions, each backed by a small stake slashed on fraud. A sybil farm can mint many vertices, but each needs its own history and stake, so attack cost scales linearly while reward per identity stays capped. Like pigment, reputation cannot be copied onto a fresh identity without redoing the work.
